title: Collins refurbishment looks like overrunning, hitting availability | The Strategist
paragraphs: Australia’s plan to extend the lives of its Collins-class submarines is quietly unravelling. While awaiting the arrival and build-up of a nuclear submarine fleet, the country is facing a high risk of downward-spiralling operational availability of its six diesel boats.
This risk is appearing despite a decision to avoid it by accepting a loss of the submarines’ future technological competitiveness.

In May 2026, the Australian National Audit Office (ANAO) delivered a sobering assessment of the Collins-class Life–of–Type Extension (LOTE) program, which is needed to keep the boats, already up to 30 years old, going into the 2030s and 2040s. The government had just revealed that LOTE would involve not modernisation but only refurbishment, and for only five of the submarines. This would keep the fleet in service with current capability.
